turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the openai-node repository structure to find streaming implementation details.Now let me find which public API methods construct/return this `Stream` class — search resources for `Stream.fromSSEResponse` usage and `stream: true` handling.Good, search works with `+` combining. Let me search for `fromSSEResponse` properly and for resource files using streaming.This is very informative. Let me look at the `create` method's core request path, and check responses.ts and completions.ts (legacy) similarly.Now let's check ChatCompletionStream and ResponseStream in lib/, plus AssistantStream for beta.threads, and audio/image streaming.Confirmed both helper classes call the low-level SDK method with `stream: true` and iterate the returned `Stream`. Now let's check the beta Assistants (`AssistantStream`), legacy `completions.ts`, and audio/image streaming for completeness.I have enough to also confirm `runs.ts` streaming and `speech.ts`/`transcriptions.ts` for completeness.I now have complete and well-verified evidence across all streaming surfaces. Here's the full picture.

## Where streaming is implemented

**Core primitive — `src/core/streaming.ts`** (re-exported by the deprecated `src/streaming.ts`)
- `class Stream<Item>` — an `AsyncIterable` wrapper around a fetch `Response`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` — parses `Response.body` as Server-Sent Events (via the internal `_iterSSEMessages`/`SSEDecoder`/`LineDecoder` helpers), JSON-parses each `data:` payload, stops at `data: [DONE]`, and throws `APIError` if a chunk contains an error.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — parses a newline-delimited JSON `ReadableStream` (used for replaying stored SSE bodies, e.g. `AssistantStream._fromReadableStream`).
- Also provides `.tee()` and `.toReadableStream()`.

**Wiring point — `src/internal/parse.ts`**, function `defaultParseResponse()`:
```ts
if (props.options.stream) {
  if (props.options.__streamClass) {
    return props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(response, props.controller, client, ...);
  }
  return Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, props.controller, client, ...);
}
```
This is the single choke point: every API call passes `stream: true/false` in `RequestOptions`, and `APIPromise` (`src/core/api-promise.ts`) calls this parser when the promise resolves. `__streamClass` lets specific endpoints substitute a custom `Stream` subclass.

**Higher-level ergonomic wrappers (in `src/lib/`)**, all built on top of `Stream`:
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` (`ChatCompletionStream`, extends `AbstractChatCompletionRunner` in `src/lib/AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts`) — accumulates chat completion chunks into a running snapshot and emits typed events (`content.delta`, `tool_calls.function.arguments.done`, etc). Its `_createChatCompletion` literally calls `client.chat.completions.create({...params, stream: true})` and iterates the resulting `Stream`.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` (`ResponseStream`, extends `EventStream` in `src/lib/EventStream.ts`) — same pattern for the Responses API; accumulates via `ResponseAccumulator.ts`.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` (`AssistantStream`, also extends `EventStream`) — used by the Assistants/Threads/Runs beta API; has both `fromReadableStream` (via `Stream.fromReadableStream`) and live-SSE creation paths.

## Public API methods that route into streaming

| Method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:61-79` | returns `APIPromise<Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(params)` | same file, `:219-225` | wraps in `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools({stream:true})` | same file, `:196-217` | wraps in `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner` |
| `client.completions.create({stream: true})` (legacy) | `src/resources/completions.ts:28-43` | `APIPromise<Stream<Completion>>` |
| `client.responses.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-122` | `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream: true})` | same file, `:137-168` | `APIPromise<Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.responses.stream(params)` | same file, `:199-205` | wraps in `ResponseStream.createResponse` |
| `client.images.generate({stream: true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:75-93` | `APIPromise<Stream<ImageGenStreamEvent>>` (partial-image events) |
| `client.images.edit({stream: true})` | same file, `:45-61` | `APIPromise<Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:43-62` | `APIPromise<Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.audio.speech.create(...)` | `src/resources/audio/speech.ts:29-35` | NOT SSE — raw binary via `__binaryResponse: true`, returns a `Response` directly (fetch body stream, not the `Stream` class) |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRun({stream: true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts:143-163` | `APIPromise<Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRunStream(...)` | same file, `:182-183` | wraps in `AssistantStream.createThreadAssistantStream` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream: true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:57-82` | `APIPromise<Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` / `.createAndStream(...)` | same file, `:165-170, 232-233` | wraps in `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` | same file, `:294-299` | wraps in `AssistantStream.createToolAssistantStream` |

Realtime (`src/resources/realtime`, `src/resources/beta/realtime`) uses a WebSocket transport, not this SSE `Stream` — a separate mechanism I did not trace in depth.

## Not verified
- I didn't inspect `src/resources/realtime/*` or `src/resources/beta/realtime/*` internals (WebSocket-based, out of scope for the SSE `Stream` class).
- I didn't check `src/internal/shims*.ts` (`ReadableStreamToAsyncIterable`, platform fetch shims) in detail — took their behavior as described by call sites.
- Content reflects the repository's current default branch at time of query (fetched via GitHub Contents API, not a pinned commit/tag) — line numbers may shift with future commits.
